deep_dive.title: LLM-Driven Joint Evolution of Coupled Heuristics Components for Routing Optimization
deep_dive.abstract: Heuristic design for combinatorial optimization remains heavily reliant on expert knowledge, while existing large language model (LLM)-enhanced evolutionary methods typically evolve isolated algorithmic components, even when one determines the search state on which another operates. This paper proposes LLM-driven Heuristic Components Joint Generation (LLM-HCJG), a population-based framework that jointly generates and co-evolves interdependent heuristic components under a shared design blueprint. Applied to guided local search (GLS), LLM-HCJG couples solution initialization with penalty construction and embeds the generated pair into an enhanced online search mechanism. The resulting form is further transferred from the traveling salesman problem (TSP) to the capacitated vehicle routing problem (CVRP). Theoretical analysis establishes the non-separable state-transition effects between the two components and the advantage in generation consistency. Across synthetic instances and 41 public TSPLIB/CVRPLIB benchmarks, LLM-HCJG attains consistently low optimality gaps, including best or tied-best results on 28 of 29 TSPLIB instances and all 12 CVRPLIB instances. Ablation and structural analyses further indicate that these gains are associated with cross-component compatibility and alignment rather than isolated-component recombination. These results support effective cross-instance transfer within the evaluated routing settings under limited-sample, modest-cost training.

deep_dive.llm_tldr_en: LLM-HCJG is an LLM-driven population framework that jointly generates and co-evolves coupled heuristic components for guided local search in routing optimization. It couples solution initialization with penalty construction and transfers generated heuristics from the traveling salesman domain, yielding stronger search performance and less manual expert design.
deep_dive.llm_tldr_cn: 当前组合优化的启发式设计高度依赖专家知识，而现有大语言模型增强的进化方法通常只进化孤立的算法组件，忽略了组件间相互依赖关系。本文提出LLM-HCJG，一种基于大语言模型的种群框架，在共享设计蓝图中联合生成并协同进化相互依赖的启发式组件，并将生成结果嵌入增强的在线搜索机制。将其应用于引导式局部搜索时，该方法把解初始化与罚构造耦合起来。在旅行商等路由问题上的迁移与对比实验表明，自动演化出的启发式配置有效提升搜索表现并减少人工设计负担，展示大模型辅助自动算法发现的潜力。

quick_skim.title: Agentic Algorithm Engineering: Improving Shared-Memory Exact Minimum Cuts
quick_skim.abstract: The minimum cut problem for an undirected edge-weighted graph asks us to divide its set of nodes into two blocks while minimizing the weighted sum of the cut edges. Over the last years, we engineered a range of fast algorithms for this problem. Our fastest exact algorithm uses an inexact algorithm to obtain a better bound for the problem, reductions that depend on this bound, improved data structures and parallel contraction routines. It is available in the open-source package VieCut and, on real-world instances, outperformed the previously fastest solvers by a factor of up to 2.5 sequentially and up to 12.9 when run in parallel. We improve this algorithm using agentic algorithm engineering (AAE), a methodology that we introduce here, in which autonomous large language model agents run the algorithm engineering cycle on an existing code base: they form hypotheses about where running time is lost, implement them, benchmark the result on a fixed instance set and keep or discard the change. Even though we had already tuned our algorithm by hand extensively, the agent finds significant optimizations, in particular on the DIMACS core instances: factors of 1.28 (sequential) and 1.63 (32 threads) on real-world k-cores, and 6.26 and 127 on the DIMACS core instances.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: AAE introduces autonomous agents to improve shared-memory exact min-cut algorithms. The improved VieCut solver is 2.5x faster sequentially and 12.9x in parallel, showing agentic workflows can automate algorithm engineering.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 针对精确最小割求解器需要大量人工算法调优、难以自动复用的瓶颈，本文提出智能体算法工程（AAE），让自主智能体自动组合约简、界改进与并行化等策略。在VieCut之上应用AAE后，改进算法在真实实例上串行提速最高2.5倍、并行最高12.9倍，优于此前最优求解器。这项工作展示了大模型或智能体驱动的自动算法工程可成为算法优化领域的一种新范式。
